Team —

Quick ask: we have an offer in motion for Jordan Lee (resume attached) for a Senior Runtime Engineer role focused on kernel/quantization work. Talent is asking for compensation above our posted E3 range; after market checks Julia recommends moving this hire to the lower half of E4 to secure acceptance.

Why this matters:
- Jordan has prior production MLOps/runtime shipping experience at scale and two published kernel patches (strong execution).
- We expect a measurable throughput/latency uplift on our long-tail workloads if Jordan can own the KV cache & attention kernel optimizations we scoped.
- Hiring risk: candidate has competing offers and requires a decision window of 72 hrs.

Ask: approval to regrade this specific headcount to E4 (one-off exception tied to candidate) and permission to draw 1 FTE from Q3 open pool (budget-neutral by moving one planned infra vacancy). Attached is a short comp-band proposal and the resume.

If we can greenlight by COB Apr 8 I will instruct Julia to send the formal offer (base + equity range in the attached draft). Please reply with approvals or questions.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Talent & People Operations
Redwood Inference

Kimberly —

Thanks for the context. A couple quick clarifying Qs before I signal thumbs-up:
1) What is the requested base + equity band you're planning to offer at E4 (range please)?
2) Can we confirm the candidate start date expectation and whether remote location impacts S/R bands?
3) On the technical side, is there a short success metric (Q/O milestone) we can tie to the comp exception to evaluate payoff?

If the base + equity stays within the low-E4 band and the start date is within Q3, I am inclined to approve in principle — Jordan’s profile aligns with the kernel priorities. Please add the numeric ranges to the comp doc and I’ll follow-up.

—Marcus
